design.affected_system: waste collection, recycling, street cleaning, illegal-dumping, and sanitation response
alternatives: screen feasible locations against the largest access gaps for sanitation depot, bin, and drop-off locations
co-optimize distributed and high-capacity locations for sanitation depot, bin, and drop-off locations

assumptions: Requests, route events, tonnage, inspections, dumping evidence, contamination, and completion remain distinct.
Waste generation and service demand are measured or modeled with declared coverage.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain only existing approved locations for sanitation depot, bin, and drop-off locations.

constraints.description: The sanitation, waste, and street cleanliness site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: sanitation commissioner and waste operations chief
design.decision_question: Where should operations and public facilities improve access while limiting traffic and environmental burdens?

design.intended_claim: A versioned site design for comparing declared alternatives affecting sanitation depot, bin, and drop-off locations, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: service demand beyond feasible sanitation facility coverage
distributional gap in service demand beyond feasible sanitation facility coverage
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a screened sanitation site permitted, safe, accepted, or built.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for sanitation depot, bin, and drop-off locations passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.

transportability_risks: Collection systems, housing form, waste law, contracts, markets, and reporting behavior differ.
